system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS Advanced mathematics test for students in the twelfth grade, the final year of secondary school, who have taken advanced mathematics courses. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
In the ΔABC the altitudes BN and CM intersect at point S. The measure of ∠MSB is 40° and the measure of ∠SBC is 20°. Write a PROOF of the following statement:

“ΔABC is isosceles.”

Give geometric reasons for statements in your proof.

[Image: Triangle ABC with altitudes BN and CM intersecting at S]

Figure, described in words:
A triangle ABC with vertex A at the top, vertex B at the bottom left, and vertex C at the bottom right. Segment BN is an altitude drawn from B to AC, with a right-angle symbol at N. Segment CM is an altitude drawn from C to AB, with a right-angle symbol at M. BN and CM intersect at interior point S. The angle MSB is marked with an arc and labeled 40°. The angle SBC is marked with an arc and labeled 20°.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Proof: Since BN is an altitude, BN ⊥ AC, so ∠BNC = 90°. Since CM is an altitude, CM ⊥ AB, so ∠CMB = 90°. In triangle BMS, ∠BMS = 90° (since M lies on AB and SM lies along CM, which is perpendicular to AB) and ∠MSB = 40° (given), so by the angle sum of a triangle, ∠MBS = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°. Since ∠SBC = 20° (given) and ∠MBC = ∠MBS + ∠SBC (because S lies inside the triangle, so ray BS lies between rays BM and BC), we get ∠ABC = ∠MBC = 50° + 20° = 70°. Now consider triangle BMC: ∠BMC = 90° (CM ⊥ AB), so ∠MCB = 180° − 90° − 70° = 20°. Since CS lies along CM, ∠SCB = ∠MCB = 20°. Thus ∠SCB = ∠SBC = 20°. Triangle SBC therefore has two equal angles at B and C, so by the converse of the isosceles triangle theorem, SB = SC. Next, we show ∠ACB = 70°: in triangle BNC, ∠BNC = 90° and ∠NBC = ∠SBC + ∠SBN; since ∠SBN is the angle in triangle SBN, we use the fact that ∠BSC = 180° − 20° − 20° = 140°, and ∠NSC is its supplement? Instead, note that ∠BSC and ∠MSB are supplementary because M, S, C are collinear: ∠BSC = 180° − ∠MSB = 180° − 40° = 140°, consistent with the above. Now in triangle BNC, ∠NBC = 90° − ∠ACB. Since ∠SCB = 20° and S lies on CM, the line CM is the altitude from C, so ∠ACM = 90° − ∠A, and in triangle AMC (right angle at M), ∠MCA = 90° − ∠A. Also, from triangle ABC, ∠A + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°, with ∠ABC = 70°, so ∠A + ∠ACB = 110°. Since ∠MCB = 20° and ∠MCA = ∠ACB − ∠MCB = ∠ACB − 20°, and ∠MCA = 90° − ∠A, we have ∠ACB − 20° = 90° − ∠A, so ∠ACB + ∠A = 110°, which is consistent but gives no new information. Instead, use BN: BN is an altitude, so in right triangle BNC, ∠NBC = 90° − ∠ACB. Since ∠NBC = ∠SBC = 20° (BN passes through S, so ray BS = ray BN), we get 90° − ∠ACB = 20°, hence ∠ACB = 70°. Since ∠ABC = 70° and ∠ACB = 70°, triangle ABC has two equal angles at B and C, so by the converse of the isosceles triangle theorem, AB = AC. Therefore ΔABC is isosceles. ∎
